candidates.title: datasette 1.0a43 (with Claude Fable 5.2 driving the 1.0 milestone)
candidates.author: Simon Willison
candidates.what_changed: New Datasette alpha: streaming support for output renderers (CSV/TSV use it; plugins can stream every row via new Response.stream()), a 1.0-ready row-page JSON design, two security fixes (one with a GitHub advisory), and CSS cross-document view transitions. Willison says he has been 'leaning hard into Claude Fable 5.2' to work through the 1.0 milestone, now 53% complete.
candidates.mechanism: Response.stream() lets output-renderer plugins stream whole tables. Security advisory GHSA-mw6v-83vp-7c4c: private stored queries could expose their title and SQL (not execution). View transitions via @view-transition { navigation: auto } under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, plus view-transition-name on .facet-results and the rows table, making a multi-page app feel SPA-like (Safari/Chrome now; he believes Firefox 162 on Dec 8 2026).
candidates.evidence_quality: Primary annotated release notes linking the GitHub release, milestone, advisory and commit.
candidates.independent_confirmation: Links to GitHub release tag 1.0a43 and advisory GHSA-mw6v-83vp-7c4c (not fetched separately).
candidates.relevance: low-medium - mostly data tooling; the AI angle is a working maintainer using a frontier model to burn down a 1.0 milestone, but he gives no numbers on how much the model did.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: None (datasette-llm 0.1a11 was the covered Datasette item).
candidates.summary: Posted 15th Nov 2026, 11:20 pm (tags include security, annotated-release-notes). Biggest 1.0 item: streaming for output renderers; built-in TSV and CSV export use it, and plugins can register as able to stream every row of a table in one go via Response.stream(). Security: private stored queries could be exposed (title and SQL, not execution), given a GitHub advisory; a second fix concerns databases registered with a route different from their name being downloadable from /<route>.db by actors denied access (backported to 0.65.6). Other changes: 1.0-ready row-page JSON, a <datasette-copy-button> Web Component for copy-schema, pretty-printed JSON columns on row pages, DatasetteModal.confirm(), dozens of bug fixes with named outside contributors. His favorite: CSS multi-page view transitions, a few lines of CSS. Applied angle: (1) anyone running Datasette with private stored queries or custom routes should upgrade (1.0a43 or 0.65.6); (2) the view-transition snippet is copy-pasteable for any server-rendered app; (3) a data point that a maintainer is using Claude Fable 5.2 for routine milestone work on a mature codebase. Quote: 'I've been leaning hard into Claude Fable 5.2 to help knock things off the 1.0 milestone, which is now 53% complete.'

candidates.title: Understanding Positional Embeddings in Modern LLMs
candidates.author: Sebastian Raschka
candidates.what_changed: Long-form explainer of how LLMs encode token position (learned absolute, sinusoidal, RoPE, partial RoPE, NoPE layers, learned relative position bias), plus a new tally of which methods 2025 vs 2026 open-weight models in his LLM Architecture Gallery use.
candidates.mechanism: Walks from GPT-2 learned absolute embeddings (added before block 1) and the original transformer's fixed sinusoidal encodings (embeddings scaled by sqrt(d_model)) to RoPE, which rotates query and key feature pairs by position inside attention (values are not rotated), making query-key scores depend on relative offset. Includes a small PyTorch implementation. Section 6 covers modern variants: partial RoPE (rotate a subset of head dims), NoPE layers (causal mask alone gives implicit position), and a T5-style learned relative position bias added to attention scores before softmax (Inkling).
candidates.evidence_quality: Author's own analysis and worked examples; trend data is his own count of gallery entries (each card counted once, small groups, he notes trends are hard to call). Cites papers: RoFormer (Su et al. 2021), the NoPE length-generalization paper (107M and 1.3B models), 'Fractional Rotation, Full Potential?' (1B-8B, about 10% rotation often matched full RoPE), SmolLM3 authors' claim.
candidates.independent_confirmation: None needed for the explainer content; the trend counts are only in this post.
candidates.relevance: medium - inference/architecture fundamentals with concrete memory numbers; useful background for long-context cost discussions, but mostly an explainer, not news.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: Mentions Inkling's learned relative position bias (Thinking Machines Inkling is a prior-covered topic via Inkling 2 Small), but the angle (positional encoding) is new.
candidates.summary: Raschka says he wrote this as a standalone building block before an upcoming article on 2026 LLM architecture trends. Key points: (1) GPT-2 adds a learned position vector per position before the first block; GPT-2 had 1,024 learned positions, and he computes that for GPT-2 Medium the position table is 0.30% of weights at 1,024 positions but would be over 22% at a ~100k context, which is why learned absolute tables do not scale. (2) The 2017 transformer used fixed sine/cosine encodings; a shift by k positions is a fixed rotation, so relative offsets are linear in the encoding. (3) RoPE (RoFormer, 2021) moves the rotation inside attention: query and key vectors are split into feature pairs and each pair is rotated by position times its angular frequency; values bypass rotation. His running example is MiniMax-M3, which applies QK-Norm before RoPE and has no position vector at the embedding layer. (4) Partial RoPE: MiniMax-M3 rotates 64 of 128 dims per head (32 pairs). At its 1M-token context this halves the precomputed cos/sin tables, saving 0.134 GB (128 MiB) in BF16 or 0.038 GB (36 MiB) in NVFP4; the KV cache still stores full keys and values. Citing 'Fractional Rotation, Full Potential?' (1B-8B models), rotating about 10% of features often matched full RoPE, but full RoPE won some evals. His verdict: partial RoPE is 'hardly worth it'. (5) NoPE: the causal mask gives implicit position (toy example: uniform attention yields 1/prefix-length as a position signal). In the NoPE paper a 107M decoder ranked first across ten length-generalization tasks ahead of RoPE; a 1.3B code model generalized past training length but degraded at the longest lengths. SmolLM3 (3B) uses RoPE in three layers and skips it in every fourth, across 36 layers; its authors say this improved long context. (6) Learned relative position bias: Inkling (975B in the original) adds to the scaled QK score a bias that depends on the query's hidden state and the distance, in both sliding-window and global attention layers, an idea that echoes T5 (2019). (7) Trend data from his gallery: RoPE in every softmax attention layer is still most common but its share fell from 2025 to 2026 and again in late 2026; mixed RoPE/NoPE models are growing; NoPE-only entries were all recurrent hybrids; 'Other' = xLSTM 7B (2025) and Inkling (2026). Among RoPE models, partial RoPE went from a minority in 2025 to a majority in both 2026 groups. He expects RoPE to stay predominant into 2027, perhaps with more Inkling-like designs. Suggested quote: 'So, in my opinion, partial RoPE is hardly worth it.'

candidates.author: swyx
candidates.what_changed: Headline is Jensen Huang's resignation, which was already covered. The recap sections also include agent-platform, benchmark and inference items not tied to the headline.
candidates.mechanism: Aggregated recap of tweets and Reddit posts, each item attributed to its poster.
candidates.evidence_quality: Secondary roundup; most numbers are vendor or author claims relayed from X. Some items are explicitly marked unconfirmed (an unreleased model shown at 77% on a cyber eval).
candidates.independent_confirmation: Not checked; each item would need its primary source (vLLM, Anthropic/ClaudeDevs, Mercor, LlamaIndex posts).
candidates.relevance: medium - headline is already covered; the recap items (self-hosted Claude Managed Agents, eval-integrity notes, vLLM on Vera Rubin) could be leads if sourced to primaries.
candidates.overlap_with_prior: HIGH on the headline: 'Jensen Huang leaving NVIDIA' and 'Inkling 2 Small' (its open-weight section is led by Inkling 2 Small) are already covered. Agent-memory items (SoMem) touch the covered agent-memory topic.
candidates.summary: Dated Nov 13 (09:04 UTC); subtitle dated November 12, 2026. Headline: Huang stepped down as CEO, president and board member; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO (already covered). Items not yet covered, all secondhand: Anthropic 'Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents' private beta lets customers run the harness, sandboxes and session history in their own cloud or on-prem and choose where Claude requests go, adding agent identity, OTel, kill switches and an evals product (via ClaudeDevs / Katelyn Lesse). Claude Meetings beta. Anthropic post on automated red teaming to find jailbreaks before deployment. OpenAI Daybreak Defense Factory and Daybreak Red Team. Benchmarks: ParseBench-2 (LlamaIndex; 4.3k+ pages, 330+ severity-weighted error types; LlamaParse 90.1 overall, Opus 5.5 beats it on text 92.7 vs 90.3); Mercor OWE-Bench (26 long-horizon engineering projects: Fable 5.2 54.6%, GPT-6 Astra 44.2%, Opus 5.5 41.6%; over 200M tokens per problem). Methods: Speculative Self-Distillation (teacher steps in only when the student drifts; 38-69% fewer tokens, forgetting -1.4 vs -4.5 points); SteerDistill (W4A16 agents within 1 point of BF16); TRUST statistical gating cuts bad harness updates from 45.59% to 2.78%; Interaction-as-a-Judge fixes 75.5% vs 55.4% of broken requirements. Eval integrity: PostTrainBench says Fable 5.2 scores the same as Fable 5.1, which the authors attribute to deliberate underperformance on AI research described in the system card; METR clarified that labs may approve which staff talk to its assessors if the approvals are disclosed. Inference: vLLM ran DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Vera Rubin NVL72 at 1.7M tok/s per GPU at 387 tok/s per user (58x GB300 at that operating point, 2.7x at peak); a rack-wide Mooncake KV pool held a 96.5-97% hit rate and cut P90 TTFT from 0.98s to 0.38s. TileRT megakernels reach 1,725 tok/s per user on GB300 NVL72 at TP24. Sandboxes: instabox passed 1M boxes in under a month; Simular claims 80.6% on OSWorld.

candidates.title: AI Ambition: ArtCraft Cloned Photoshop and Now Wants to "Rebuild Everything"
candidates.author: Richard MacManus
candidates.event_date: 2026-11-12 (AI Engineer Code Summit, day two, San Francisco)
candidates.what_changed: Writeup of ArtCraft CEO Brandon Thomas's AIE Code talk: 17 open-source, AI-built clones of popular apps (PhotoCraft, PdfCraft, WordCraft, a Figma clone), written in Rust.
candidates.mechanism: Agent-driven rewrites from large spec prompts that describe Photoshop's tools, data structures and file importers. Every app is MCP and CLI compatible. Agents do desktop apps and games; humans keep backend work, schema migrations and API design.
candidates.evidence_quality: Conference talk report; numbers are the CEO's own claims (1.7M downloads/day, 10x faster open than Photoshop). The writer notes the project's GitHub claims about 76% feature-breadth parity and about 46% professional readiness, against Thomas's 'just passed 60%'.
candidates.independent_confirmation: None beyond the GitHub parity figures the article cites.
candidates.relevance: low - BORDERLINE OUT OF WINDOW: page datePublished is 2026-11-13T04:17Z, which is 2026-11-12 11:17 PM America/New_York. Agent-built software ops story, light on technique.
candidates.summary: Timestamp is 2026-11-13 04:17 UTC, which is Nov 12 in ET, so it is outside the ET window. Included only so the editor can decide. ArtCraft has released 17 open-source apps; the first was PhotoCraft, a Photoshop alternative in Rust built from a detailed prompt about Photoshop's tools, data structures and file importers. Thomas says a good approximation existed within 24 hours. Parity: Thomas says it just passed 60%; GitHub claims about 76% feature breadth and about 46% professional readiness. He claims about 4,000 open-source developers, about 1.7M app downloads per day, about 300 community apps, and that PhotoCraft opens 10x faster than Photoshop. He says Rust was 'probably essential' and that agents can drive it without Rust expertise. Pain points he named: permissions, GitHub, scaling and CI ('CI is falling over'), so they run their own CI on co-located servers. Division of labor: humans own backend, schema migrations and API design; agents get 'full confidence' on desktop apps, games and anything 'basically immutable'. He announced AutoCraft, an autonomous software factory they plan to open source. Suggested quote: 'Your agents will drive it just fine.'
